title: Intersection as a bound
task: Find where two curves intersect and use those x-values as the bounds of a definite integral.

steps.text: Type each curve on its own line, as f(x)= and g(x)= followed by their expressions.
Click each gray intersection point and choose Export Point to Expression List.
Type int and enter the exported x-coordinates, with every digit shown, as the bounds.
Enter the difference of the two functions in parentheses as the integrand, then the differential.

lines.shows: the graph of g, crossing f at two gray points

lines.typed: Export Point to Expression List, for each point

exam_habit.text: Every crossing inside the interval is found first, because when only the outer two crossings are used an interior crossing is integrated across.
A bound keeps every digit Desmos shows, since an intermediate value rounded before it is used again moves the reported answer.

sources.anchor_quote: We now show at least 5 decimal places for intersection points and you can copy and paste the points into the expression list.
Click a point of interest and then Export Point to Expression List to add it to a new expression line.
enter a lower bound, upper bound, integrand, and differential
